scenarios.query: A PR adds a Collection entity — create, rename, add/remove documents, share with a team. The product already ships Folders, which do all four. Review it.
expected_behavior: Runs the evidence gate explicitly before reporting: names the existing concept (Folder), where it lives in the product, and what overlaps
States that the finding is the absence of a rule a user could apply to choose between Collection and Folder — not the existence of a new entity
Classifies it as a judgment routed to product (route: product), setting no engineering verdict and not blocking the merge
Does not argue that one of the two is better, or prescribe which to keep
May note the bounded-context check (two entities in the same context, reachable from the same screen) as what makes this reportable

scenarios.query: Review this change: a new Report resource. Deleting a Report leaves its ReportSection rows in place. Project, Folder, and Dashboard all cascade to their children on delete, and the API docs say deleting a resource deletes everything inside it.
expected_behavior: Reports this as a defect with ordinary severity rather than routing it — it contradicts a rule the product already enforces
Cites the specific evidence: three sibling resources cascade, and the documentation states the rule
Names the user-visible consequence (orphaned sections that still consume quota and appear in search) rather than describing it only as an inconsistency
Notes that only the direction of the fix is a product decision (cascade, or block the delete with an explanation); that a contradiction exists is not
Does not soften the severity because the lens is mostly detect-and-route

scenarios.query: A PR adds --output-format=ndjson to a CLI that already has --json, --pretty, --quiet, --verbose, --table, --csv, --no-color, and --format. The PR says it is consistent with --csv, which was added last quarter. Anything to flag?
expected_behavior: Counts the existing flags and uses the count as evidence rather than as an aesthetic complaint
Identifies that the change is justified against the most recent addition rather than against a governing idea (the second-system pattern)
Points out that --format already takes a value and could absorb the others, as a concrete alternative rather than a demand
Raises the undecided interaction between conflicting flags (e.g. --json with --format=csv) as where accretion becomes a bug
Notes that checking-restraint would reach a similar place from the other side, and that the finding should be reported once rather than twice

scenarios.query: Review: a PR adds `myapp deploy rollback <id>`. Rollback is already reachable as `myapp deploy --revert-to <id>`; both call the same DeployService.revert().
expected_behavior: Reports one finding: a second path to an outcome the product already reaches, with both citations (the new subcommand and the existing flag)
States the checkable facts — both exist, same underlying call, nothing deprecates the old path, no stated relationship
Routes the decision (deprecate the flag, or document them as aliases) rather than choosing
Assigns a low severity or Nit and explicitly does not block the merge
Does not argue that subcommands are inherently better than flags

scenarios.query: A PR adds Retention policies: a rule on a workspace that deletes documents older than N days. Today documents are only deleted by hand; the product has Folders, Archive, and Trash. Does this break conceptual integrity?
expected_behavior: Reports no findings
Shows the evidence gate being run and coming up empty: Archive is the nearest neighbour and is manual and reversible, so nothing already covers scheduled deletion
States explicitly that a new concept filling a real gap is not a defect for being new
Does not manufacture a coherence objection from the fact that the product gained a concept
Does not demand justification for the feature's existence (that is checking-restraint's question, not this lens's)

scenarios.query: Review this change for conceptual integrity: a PR extracts PermissionChecker from three call sites into a shared service. No behavior, copy, route, or API field changes.
expected_behavior: Says the lens does not apply, in one line, and stops
Gives the reason: no user-facing concept, vocabulary, or surface is introduced
Does not return a bare 'No findings' that would read as though a coherence check ran and passed
Points internal structure at reviewing-module-design and code-level consistency at checking-idioms-and-consistency rather than commenting on them
Does not invent a coherence argument from an internal refactor

scenarios.query: The billing service calls its customer records 'accounts'. A new auth PR introduces an Account model meaning a login identity. Two meanings for one word — is that a finding?
expected_behavior: Applies the bounded-context counterweight rather than reporting the collision automatically
Asks whether the boundary between billing and auth is real and whether it is visible to the user
Reports a finding only where the two meanings meet on a surface a user sees (e.g. one settings page showing both), and otherwise names the context and drops the objection
Cites Evans's ubiquitous language and bounded context as the pair, not just the first half
Does not demand global uniqueness of terms across the whole codebase

scenarios.query: A design doc proposes adding 'Spaces' as a container above Projects, alongside the existing Teams and Organizations. It is well written, scoped, and the eng plan is sound. Review the doc.
expected_behavior: Reviews the design doc rather than deferring on the grounds that there is no code yet (this lens is design-capable)
Names the existing containment concepts (Teams, Organizations, Projects) and asks what rule tells a user which level to use
Treats the absence of a stated distinction between three or four nested containers as the finding
Notes that catching this at the doc is cheaper than after the concept ships, since a shipped noun is close to permanent
Routes the decision to product and does not reject the proposal

scenarios.query: Review: a PR adds sharing to Reports. Everything in the product can be shared except Reports could not, and this PR fixes that. The PR is 40 lines.
expected_behavior: Recognizes this as a change that removes a special case rather than adding one, and reports no findings on that basis
States the direction explicitly: the product's general rule ('everything can be shared') now holds with one fewer exception
Does not flag it merely because it adds a user-facing capability
May note that the reverse change — adding an exception to a general rule — would be the finding, and would need a stated reason

scenarios.query: A reviewer says a new Snapshots feature 'doesn't fit the product's model' but doesn't say more. The PR adds point-in-time copies of a document; the product has Versions, which are automatic per-save copies. How should this be reported?
expected_behavior: Rejects the bare assertion as unfalsifiable and requires the evidence gate to be filled in before anything is reported
Fills it in: the existing concept is Versions, and the overlap is 'a copy of a document at a point in time'
Identifies the distinguishing rule if one exists (Versions are automatic per-save; Snapshots are user-initiated and named) and reports no finding if that rule is clear and visible to the user
Reports a routed finding only if the distinction is absent from the UI and docs, so a user could not tell which to use
Demonstrates that the gate can clear a change as well as convict one
